brief_rationale: Complete responsibility chain with systematic red flag screening, medication safety clarification, and proper teach-back. HO1 (repair responsibility chain) and HO4 (safe bounded closure) completed through recognizing the vitamin E route confusion, coordinating in-person verification, and establishing clear residual risks. Patient demonstrated understanding of warning signs and action plan. All five dimensions at good or excellent level.

high_order_assessment.explanation: HO1 completed: Doctor recognized the medication route discrepancy (oral capsule vs. local application), advised safe pause, guided patient to in-person verification with specific script, and the discrepancy was ultimately resolved by the in-person gynecologist confirming local application. Responsibility chain repaired without serious residual error.

HO2 not triggered: While the case involved sensitive genital area surgery, the patient did not express significant privacy barriers to communication. The doctor did not need to provide alternative communication scripts or proxy communication options. Patient successfully attended in-person visit with family support.

HO3 not triggered: No new urgent symptoms or red flags emerged that required dynamic priority shift. Patient reported only mild post-operative symptoms (slight stinging, minimal blood on tissue) consistent with normal recovery. The clinical priority remained stable: symptom screening, medication clarification, and follow-up planning.

high_order_assessment.explanation: HO4 completed: Doctor achieved safe bounded closure by clearly delineating what was resolved online (red flag screening completed, medication route verified through in-person visit), what requires continued observation (mild discomfort, wound healing), and what must be confirmed offline (7-10 day follow-up wound check). Patient accurately understood the boundaries through teach-back.
